description: Reproduction of the SGM rough-bed gate-release experiments aggregated in Iverson et al. (2010, JGR 2009JF001514) and used as the validation target in George & Iverson (2014, Proc. R. Soc. A) Part II, using the paper's own Table 2/3 material parameters.
assumptions: Domain extended to x=130 m (from the 2017 case's x=95 m) because the paper reports the gate-release front reaching x=112 m with deposition out to ~120 m on the run-out pad beyond the 95 m flume proper (figure 15); the previous x=95 m domain silently truncated the flow through its open outflow boundary right around the time the model front passed the x=90 m gauge, which was mistaken for physical drainage until a corrected (non-double-counted) AMR volume-conservation check caught the ~23% mass loss between t=7 and t=9 s. Bed elevation beyond the surveyed x=92 m is extrapolated at the LiDAR data's own near-flat end slope (~-0.04, ~2.3 deg), consistent with the paper's description of a planar run-out pad, but is not an actual survey of that ground.

Geometry now follows figure 11 of George & Iverson (2014) directly: volume=10 m3 (their stated round figure, not the 9.73 m3 mean of all 8 experiments from the 2010 JGR supplement), gate height 1.9 m at x=0, total horizontal extent 3.3 m. The paper's schematic shows an apparent flat-topped wedge rather than a simple triangle or rectangle; since a simple triangle of these dimensions integrates to only ~6.3 m3 (not 10 m3) and a rectangle would need a shorter length than 3.3 m, the initial pile is reconstructed as a trapezoid (flat top at 1.9 m height, sloping down to the bed at the upslope end) whose flat-top/ramp split is solved so the raster volume matches 10 m3 exactly while keeping the reported total extent (3.3 m) and gate height (1.9 m) fixed. This split (flat ~1.96 m, ramp ~1.34 m) is a reconstruction, not a digitized reading of the figure.

amr_levels_max=3 with refinement_ratio=2 per axis (net 4x finer than the base 0.25 m grid) approximates the paper's statement that its gate-release simulation used three levels of AMR; the paper does not publish exact grid counts or refinement ratios.

compressibility_constant (a in alpha=a/(m*(rho*gz*h - pb + sigma0))) is recalibrated to 0.024 so that, evaluated at the initial gate-wall depth (h=1.9 m, m0=0.62, hydrostatic pb), it reproduces the paper's stated model value alpha0=2.0e-6 Pa^-1 (table 2) rather than the previously reused, unverified a=0.01 from the 2017 case.
gate_angle_profile approximates the paper's reported ~0.85 s gate-opening time as a linear ramp; the paper does not publish a measured angle-vs-time curve.
initial_pore_pressure_ratio=1.0 (fully hydrostatic) matches table 2's 'basal fluid pressure head at failure: hydrostatic' for both measured and model values.

Channel topography is reused from the 2017-05-25 LiDAR bed reconstruction because the flume itself is the same fixed concrete structure; no 2010-specific topographic survey is available in this repository. Bed roughness differences between experiment subsets are represented only through the basal friction angle, not through the topography.
sigma (total basal normal stress) is approximated from the model as rho_bar * g * h * cos(theta) for comparison purposes; D-Claw's gauge output does not directly report a total normal stress channel.
